records.region: Coquimbo, Chile; unnamed southeastern head branch, Ortega–Chicharra–Choapa corridor and coastal terminal.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Completed bounded representative receiving-system identity; the unnamed headward branch, Estero de Ortega and Río de la Chicharra remain distinct natural reaches. No uniform name is assigned to every selected reach or terminal waterbody.
records.completion_scope: All 39 selected parts of FID14040, the actual chosen unnamed opening, the Ortega and Chicharra transitions, all intermediate selected Choapa reaches and meaningful tributary joins, the coastal receiving wetland/lagoon connection and actual ending were inspected in complete bounded MMA originals. Returned IGM lines supply bounded supporting reach attributes only. No meaningful selected connection remains unestablished at ordinary corridor scale.
records.supported_name_scope: Completed bounded representative receiving-system identity; the unnamed headward branch, Estero de Ortega and Río de la Chicharra remain distinct natural reaches. No uniform name is assigned to every selected reach or terminal waterbody.

component_scope_limits: Blank headward source attributes do not establish that no local or official name exists.
The separate Del Valle, Arco del Choapa and Agua Fria tributaries are not names for the chosen upstream branch.
Ortega and Chicharra are direct reach names, not aliases imposed on the entire system.
The wetland inventory label Rio Illapel is retained as a source-specific naming conflict/grouping; it is not adopted as the Choapa river name.
Source survey epoch, numeric scale, present flow and shoreline are not verified.

records.region: Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil; Cerro Corá–São Tomé–Barcelona–São Paulo do Potengi–São Pedro–Ielmo Marinho–São Gonçalo do Amarante–Natal
records.candidate_name_role: Supported natural-river corridor candidate; not a completed representative identity for the entire selected synthetic system.
records.material_pending_reason: The actual final selected estuary-to-coast extension lacks a source-supported continuous water link. General estuarine proximity and repeated inland Potengi names do not establish it. Three unavailable independent sources supplied no usable terminal map; their outcomes remain factual reasons, not additional primary statuses.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Potengi in Rio Grande do Norte, reaching the Natal estuarine setting. This is not the Ceará locality Potengi, another coastal river, or an accepted name for every synthetic selected part.
records.completion_scope: All supplied encoded parts considered against available regional cartography. Inland trunk correspondence and named receiving setting are supported at ordinary regional scale; the final through-link remains material pending. No exact bank/vertex, present tidal branch, current flow or operating-condition proof is demanded.
records.supported_name_scope: The acquired regional original repeatedly labels the continuous inland river Potengi; the separate primary spring study corroborates its Cerro Corá/Serra de Santana headwater setting and general Atlantic destination.

scope_limits: Exact natural spring corresponding to the selected start is unverified; source-site names are not automatically assigned to a selected start.
Regional cartographic generalization does not establish every small impoundment, road crossing or tidal-channel detail. No additional named lake/reservoir identity is assigned.

The final selected extension cannot be certified as a river/estuary connection from the acquired original. Its apparent relation to the urban strip needs independent usable geographic evidence, not an exact shoreline test.
Unacquired sources provide no substantive map/prose observations. The UFRN repository item’s full title, verified author and publication year remain unknown.
No single accepted scalar name, Korean name, formal registry status, present hydraulics or operating condition is established.

bounded_name_observations.name: Rio Potengi
bounded_name_observations.role: Supported natural inland trunk and Natal receiving setting only; the selected final estuary-to-coast connection remains unestablished.

records.region: Kitikmeot, Nunavut, Canada; selected western lake-chain approach, Western River and the southern head of Bathurst Inlet.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The chosen western feeder joins the Western River and the connected southern/eastern lake loop, then follows the northward receiving river into Bathurst Inlet. Beechey Lake is the 76G sheet title and a separate regional lake, not a name for the selected opening. Bathurst Lake lies west of the lower selected river; the model does not cross that lake. The project’s winter ice road is also a separate mapped feature. Lower-course labels and terminal prose support Western River as representative identity; they do not rename every feeder or lake.
records.completion_scope: Ordinary corridor-scale correspondence covers every part of the single selected mainstem fragment: the chosen northwestern lake opening, southwest feeder and its join, the southern lake bend, eastward connected lake/channel sequence, the northward named river, overlapping northern continuation and the actual receiving head of Bathurst Inlet. No material missing through-link remains at this scale. This establishes a bounded representative system identity, without an exact-bank, vertex, present-flow or uniform-name claim.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected selected system from the named Western River corridor and its Bathurst Inlet outlet. The chosen unnamed opening, feeder lakes and intermediate lake passages are not assigned Western River as one uniform scalar name.

bounded_name_observations.name: Western River
bounded_name_observations.role: Completed representative identity with unnamed selected feeder and lake passages.

bounded_name_observations.name: Kilokgiktok (Western River)
bounded_name_observations.role: Source-specific lower-river label in the 2019 project map; not promoted to a verified alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Bathurst Inlet
bounded_name_observations.role: Receiving coastal head, distinct from unselected Bathurst Lake.

records.region: Alabama–Mississippi, Escatawpa River and lower Pascagoula River corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Completed bounded representative Escatawpa River identity for the selected Escatawpa-dominated corridor, with the final receiving Pascagoula River component explicitly preserved. This is not one natural name for every selected reach.
records.completion_scope: Four original USGSTopo views and thirteen overlapping original-pixel corridor crops establish ordinary geographic correspondence of the sole selected FID9977 from its northern Escatawpa opening through the full named trunk, meaningful tributary joins, lower broad-water/Moss Point passage, Escatawpa–Pascagoula junction and actual selected lower-Pascagoula waterfront terminal. No concrete missing selected through-link remains at this bounded scale. Distinct names remain separate, and the final generalized riverside position is not treated as an exact mouth or bank.
records.supported_name_scope: Escatawpa River from the chosen northern opening through the long Alabama–Mississippi corridor to Moss Point; Pascagoula River for the receiving lower channel and actual selected terminal.

scope_limits: Formal registry status, official name-boundary vertices, Indigenous-name equivalence and Korean forms were not investigated.
A representative Escatawpa identity does not rename the receiving Pascagoula River component or adjacent named lakes.
The chosen opening is not an official river-source claim, and the modeled length is not an official river length.

The source establishes ordinary connected river corridors. Selected generalized lines cut individual meanders and reach local riverside ground; no exact bank, bend or confluence vertex agreement is asserted.
The actual selected endpoint is beside the lower Pascagoula city waterfront, north of the open bay outlet; the finding does not move it to an offshore Gulf terminal.
Cartography is not evidence of present flow, tidal direction, navigability or operations. The metadata refresh is not a uniform survey date.

bounded_name_observations.name: Escatawpa River
bounded_name_observations.role: Representative identity of the dominant selected corridor, ending at its distinct receiving-river confluence.

bounded_name_observations.name: Pascagoula River
bounded_name_observations.role: Separate downstream receiving component and actual selected waterfront terminal; not renamed Escatawpa.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
